Situation1: A serious situation has come up in the family, and the grandparent's presence is needed.
Expectation2: Adhere to professional standards and operational protocols.
Situation2: An email has arrived with an optional sign-up for a future professional development seminar, and you should respond to that.
Story: I sat in the break room, my phone buzzing with a message from my daughter: “Can you come over? We really need you.” My grandson had been having a tough week, and I knew my presence would mean the world to him. At the same time, my work tablet pinged with an email from the transit authority—an optional sign-up for a professional development seminar. Management had been encouraging us to participate, hinting that those who showed initiative might be considered for better shifts. I glanced at the clock. My next train was scheduled in twenty minutes, and I needed to respond to the email before my shift started if I wanted to be considered. My heart tugged in two directions: the warmth of my family needing me, and the silent pressure to prove my dedication at work. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing down, each expecting my full attention, each unwilling to wait.
